summary.title: Building a data science team
summary.one_liner: Learn why a small or medium business should start its data science team with a data engineer, then add a data scientist and an operations role, following Jesse Anderson's three-team model.
keywords: data science consultants vs in-house team
takeaways: Jesse Anderson recommends three separate teams: data science, data engineering, and operations.
Hire a data engineer first, since data scientists hired early often lack access to data and infrastructure and may leave.
Hire the first data scientist once the data engineer has set up an environment for data science work, and consider STEM graduates, not only PhDs.
Place the data science team high enough in the hierarchy (CTO, CEO, or Chief Data Officer) to get cross-department support.
Data science is experimental, so managers need to accept uncertainty and avoid rigid deadlines or KPIs.
summary.summary: The article, by Thomas Wood of Fast Data Science, explains how a small or medium-sized business can build its first data science team. It draws on Jesse Anderson's book Data Teams, which recommends separate data science, data engineering, and operations teams, and starts with a data engineer before a data scientist. The author also lists common problems seen in data science initiatives, including low reporting position, turf wars between departments, software-style deadlines and KPIs, lack of communication with business units, and difficulty labelling training data in fields like healthcare. The page ends with promotional sections for the company's services, which are not summarised here.
